sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Hemmingen, a town south of Hannover, is known for the Stadtbahn that now ends at its edge, and what policy we found is about public transport and about one street. We found no town-level parking-fee statute, parking-disc zones, resident parking or parking-space statute; the town's list of statutes shows none, which cannot prove that no parking rules exist, and its council information system was behind a bot check. The town's draft transport development plan of September 2018, a consultant report, aims to strengthen public transport, cycling and park-and-ride links, and planned 196 car spaces and a covered bike facility with 48 racks at the future Stadtbahn terminus [0]. For the Hoher Holzweg in Arnum it counted 129 existing kerbside spaces and compared redesign variants that would leave between 54 and 96 of them, because a continuous two-lane road is needed as a feeder to the new B 3, with about 35 to 40 replacement bays on green strips; these are options in a draft, not decisions [1]. The same plan proposed public charging posts first at the Real supermarket in Hemmingen-Westerfeld and near the town hall [2]. The town's cycling concept of 2015 aimed to lift the cycling share from 12 percent to at least 18 percent by 2025 [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Stadtbahn extension is the development. Line 13 from Oberricklingen to Hemmingen, 3.3 km with six new stops and a cost of about 90 million euros, was opened with a ceremony on 9 November 2023 and runs between Hemmingen and Fasanenkrug from the timetable change on 10 December 2023, with bus connections adapted [4][5]. At the opening the infra reported about 9,200 residents and 5,300 jobs in the catchment of the six stops, and the mayor called the line, together with the B 3 bypass, the biggest infrastructure project ever realised in the town [8]. The park-and-ride at the terminus was planned in 2014 with about 200 spaces [3], and was built with 170 car spaces, five of them extra large for wheelchair users, with initially seven equipped for electric charging; it can later be extended eastwards on land already bought [4][6]. A covered bike-and-ride facility was released for use on 10 June 2026, and on 28 August 2026 the Region said its lockable part was open, with 75 lockable spaces and 215 bike spaces in total, free after a one-time registration [14][15]. Planning for a further Stadtbahn extension to Arnum was stepped up in 2022, with two new stops and, as a plan, a council principle decision in spring 2023 and a funding application in 2024; we did not check anything after 2022 [9].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The park-and-ride and bike-and-ride belong to the infra, the Region Hannover's infrastructure company, and the state paid 1.3 million euros towards the P+R, B+R and bus interchange facilities [7]. The infra says its park-and-ride sites in the network are free of charge but reserved for GVH passengers, with a maximum stay of 22 hours and a contractual penalty of 50 euros a day for misuse, checked by a service company [12]. It lists Hemmingen with 170 car spaces among 20 sites with more than 2,000 spaces in total [13]. An infra manager said in March 2024, in an article about a different location, that the Hemmingen park-and-ride is often fully booked, a passing remark without occupancy figures [11].

Our data cover the Hemmingen park-and-ride, with 170 spaces, for about 27 days since late September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 33% on weekdays and 16% at weekends, which fits a commuter car park, with a single reading at 89% late on a Thursday morning. That is lower than the 2024 remark suggests, though it was two years earlier and may refer to peaks.
